newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty, central bank to lock horns next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty, central bank to lock horns next week.

text.p: The zloty is poised to fight a lost battle against the central bank on Monday as foreign entry into T-bills and banks' currency position cutting are likely to again pit it against currency-buying interventions.
Dealers said foreign investors, eager to lock into high Polish T-bill yields amid falling inflation, would boost demand at Monday's 1.3 billion zloty tender and depress yields.
But dealers were mixed on the size of foreign entry.

"I would expect foreign demand to be at similar levels as last Monday, when it amounted to 1.7 billion zlotys, and just as last week, they might buy most of what is on offer," said Bartlomiej Kumela of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
But others said that although foreigners were likely to come to the Monday tender, their interest was now more likely to turn to the 800 million zloty fixed bond auction on May 7.
"I would expect foreign bids at $100-150 million on Monday as the coming fixed bond tender will offer yet more attractive instruments," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers expected the 52-week yield on Monday to ease to 21.50-60 percent from 21.68 percent at the last tender.
They saw the 26-week and 13-week yield down to 21.50 percent from 21.69 and 21.74 percent respectively with the 8-week paper down to 21.30 percent from 21.46 percent.
Dealers said foreign bids at the T-bill tender would propel the zloty upward, above levels at which the central bank is certain step in with currency purchases.

The National Bank of Poland (NBP) said on Wednesday it wanted the zloty no higher than at 2.5 percent from the daily trading band centre after it pounded it for five days in a row with interventions whenever it peeked above that level.

Dealers said that although only part of the foreign bids would come from new forex operations as many investors were long on zlotys from deals done earlier this week and last week, the upward pressure on Polish unit would be strong.

"On Monday there will be the T-bill tender with foreign entry, but also banks will be cutting their own currency positions to keep higher yielding zlotys over the long weekend," said Karol Zaluski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Next Thursday and Friday are market holidays in Poland.
"These two factors combined are likely to trigger an intervention to stop the zloty's rise," Zaluski said.
On Friday the zloty around 2.47 percent from the parity rate, nearly flat from last week's close at 2.5 percent.
Dealers also expected large liquidity swings on the money market on Monday and Tuesday -- the last two days of the April required reserve period.
Spreads on one-day rates widened to 5.0/21.0 percent on Friday amid excess liquidity, not alleviated by the central bank's 343 million zloty reverse repo and a 750 million zloty NBP-bill sale.
